textbookText: Nikolaas Tinbergen, a Nobel laureate, pioneered the study of animal behavior. His research on fixed action patterns revealed instinctive behaviors triggered by specific stimuli. Tinbergen's work in animal communication and navigation, notably in bees and birds, revolutionized ethology. His contributions reshaped our understanding of animals' cognitive abilities and adaptive behaviors in their natural environments.
